plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A hybrid flowering cherry tree producing clouds of delicate, almond-scented blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted ornamental cherry in Japan and in cities such as Washington, D.C.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Eastern United States, Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The bloom lasts only about one to two weeks, and the Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) celebrates this fleeting beauty.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems. Hundreds of cultivars bloom in spring across gardens and commercial fields, often peaking in early to mid-April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (March to May) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Netherlands, Turkey, Northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: During the 1630s Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose magenta-pink flowers burst directly from bare branches and even the trunk, followed by heart-shaped leaves. It is an important early nectar source for native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Ontario to northern Mexico
plants.funFact: The flowers are edible and have a mildly tangy flavor, and they are often added to salads.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves and large clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some trees bloom irregularly or lingeringly into autumn, while in tropical regions flowering begins around this time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (Sept to Dec) in the Southern Hemisphere, with spring to early summer blooms in the tropics and warm Northern regions starting around April to June
plants.location: Native to South America, widely planted in Australia, South Africa, India, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas line the streets and give the city the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
